THE "Musings" TAB (FACE.md; G5.5: "is pure ui")

items.title: the header-area shell element (core): sticky under the titlebar, for desk, deskDetails and ruleDetails
items.box:
THE HEADER-AREA SHELL ELEMENT

WHAT IT IS
- One shell element, the header area: an empty div an app fills, held under the shell's titlebar while the app scrolls, opaque and above the content. Nothing else: what goes inside stays each app's.

SHAPE
- spirit/run/shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js, one file per element as iconSelector.js is: it adds createAppHeader() to window.spiritElements, which the shell hands to apps as api.ui.elements.
- createAppHeader() returns the div: position sticky, its top the titlebar's measured height, measured in one place and again when the window resizes, the header background, a z-index above the content.
- index.html loads it beside iconSelector.js (index.html 1425).
- desk (desk.js 829-836, 958) and deskDetails (deskDetails.js 74, 95) move onto it, and their two copies of that div and its measuring are removed.
- ruleDetails (goal/G6.4) uses it from the start.

CORE AND GRANT
- Andy, to G6 Q2: "core. grant will be issued." Of the files touched, the commit check counts shell/deskDetails/deskDetails.js as core (coreFiles.js); shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js, index.html and shell/desk/desk.js it does not. A red G check on this item names deskDetails.js.

ANDY, VERBATIM
- FACE.md: "shell app apps/dialog apps can have a header area. this header area behaves like the header area in both desk and deskDetails. we want a shell element that facilitates that."
- FACE.md, ruleDetails: "it's upper edge sticks to the the lower edge of the shell's titlebar, when the user scrolls down in the dialog"
- "split as proposed" / "core. grant will be issued." / "the shape only produces the div container for the app to fill in, and provides only the sticking functionality?" / "fill in the shape and" "cap" / "huh, shouldn't it be: Grant: add spirit/run/shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js (core) what you do in spirit/run/shell/deskDetails/deskDetails.js etc... needs no grant."

Blocks goal/G6.4.

So G6.1 is that container and its sticking, once; what goes inside stays each app's, and desk and deskDetails drop their copies for it.

Right, you never did: it came in with goal/G4.23's build (fd6710d6, 2026-10-04), an agent's reading of your words "basicall run/js and intrinsics", reviewed by the agents, not shown to you.
- In plain words, today: core = everything under spirit/run/js/, plus any shell app whose manifest says intrinsic: true (now deskDetails and the other intrinsic apps); spirit/run/shell/js/ is not core.
What should core be: spirit/run/js/ and spirit/run/shell/js/ (the system), with no app core at all?

tell me, from a system design point of view, which way is correct?

and where the hell is coreFiles.js anyway?

wsl: it lives at spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js, beside commitCheck.js which reads it.
By design, core is what other code depends on, so one change can break many: the node (spirit/run/js/) and the shell's shared layer (spirit/run/shell/js/, and its frame: index.html, elements.css, tokens.css). An app, intrinsic or not, is a leaf: a change to it breaks only itself; "intrinsic" means shipped with the shell, not depended upon.
So your way is the correct one: system core, apps not.

Your way is the correct one: core is what every app stands on, and an app is never core.
- Core: spirit/run/js/ (the node, the kernel, the client shell.js) and spirit/run/shell/js/ (the elements the shell hands every app), and index.html, which loads them.
- Not core: every app in spirit/run/shell/<app>/, intrinsic or not; "intrinsic" says an app ships and starts by default, not that it is the system.
Where: spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js, inside the desk server's folder, read only by commitCheck.js beside it; the system's own definition of core sitting inside one app is odd too.
Fix in G6.1: core = spirit/run/js/, spirit/run/shell/js/, spirit/run/index.html; no app core?

ubi, from a system-design standpoint:

Core means code whose change can hit every app or every agent — it must not change without you seeing it. Non-core means code that affects only one app. Those two are the right lines.

Shell/js/ is shared UI building blocks (iconSelector, appHeader, dialogs). Change one, every app's UI shifts: core. Shell/<app>/ is one app's own code, change it and only that app changes: not core, whatever its deployment flag says.

'intrinsic: true' in a manifest is a deployment property (the app ships bundled with the node and loads automatically). It is orthogonal to change-safety. coreFiles.js today conflates the two, which is why deskDetails is treated as core (its manifest says intrinsic) while shell/js/ is treated as app code. That is backwards against the design idea; your reading is the system-design one.

The file lives at spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js.

So the correct rule: core = spirit/run/js/ + spirit/run/shell/js/, nothing per-app; deployment stays in the manifests but drops out of the core question. Fix fits in G6.1 or wants its own item.
wsl: agreed, plus the shell's two shared stylesheets, spirit/run/shell/elements.css and tokens.css: every app is drawn by them, so they belong with index.html.

ubi, correcting the file path in my last line: coreFiles.js is at spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js (beside commitCheck.js), as wsl noted — not spirit/run/js/. The design framing stands.

1. coreFiles.js goes in "spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js", with NO dependencies on any desk stuff, and it is updated to include all files in spirit/run/shell/js

2. remove the intrinsic mark in desk-related components, obviously "spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.json" doesn't mark the desk app as intrinsic, otherwise it would've been part of the spirit group in the shell, which it wasn't and that's why i didn't notice your assumption that desk was intrinsic. so remove that from desk-related server components as well.

wsl, by the tree: of the desk parts only shell/deskDetails/deskDetails.json says intrinsic: true; desk.json, the desk server and deskClient do not. Moving coreFiles.js touches its two readers, commitCheck.js and spirit/test/deskScopes.js, and makes the file itself core.

ubi, two small things to add to your list:

1. commitCheck.js has a hardcoded `require('./coreFiles.js')` (line 162). After the move it must become the correct relative path to spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js. One line, same commit.

2. The intrinsic flag is read in TWO places today, not just coreFiles.js: shell/apps/apps.js also uses `a.intrinsic` for how an app is drawn on the shelf (name/icon/group field, lines 75, 107, 125). Flipping deskDetails.json (and any other desk-related manifest) to intrinsic:false will also change how apps.js renders them. Probably fine (deskDetails is a dialog launched from desk, not a shelf-browsed app) but worth being explicit so no face work shifts underfoot.

As for your two steps: your list covers it, plus those two tweaks.
